      - generic
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Following up with a real fix for modern kernels, since "
          - code
            - StaticText "androidboot.use_memfd=1"
          - StaticText " alone didn't resolve it for me (still got "
          - code
            - StaticText "no ashmem-memfd compat support"
          - StaticText " from the kernel)."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Root cause on kernel 6.17: "
          - code
            - StaticText "ashmem_linux"
          - StaticText " (from "
          - code
            - StaticText "remote-android/redroid-modules"
          - StaticText ") doesn't compile against recent kernels — three real API removals:"
        - list
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "1. "
            - code
              - StaticText "mm->get_unmapped_area"
            - StaticText " member removed → replaced by the free function "
            - code
              - StaticText "mm_get_unmapped_area()"
            - StaticText " ("
            - code
              - StaticText "linux/sched/mm.h"
            - StaticText ")"
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "2. "
            - code
              - StaticText "vma->vm_flags"
            - StaticText " is now read-only → needs "
            - code
              - StaticText "vm_flags_clear()"
            - StaticText "/"
            - code
              - StaticText "vm_flags_set()"
            - StaticText " ("
            - code
              - StaticText "linux/mm.h"
            - StaticText ")"
          - listitem [level=1]
            - ListMarker "3. "
            - StaticText "The shrinker API was reworked → "
            - code
              - StaticText "register_shrinker()"
            - StaticText "/"
            - code
              - StaticText "unregister_shrinker()"
            - StaticText " on a static struct replaced by "
            - code
              - StaticText "shrinker_alloc()"
            - StaticText "/"
            - code
              - StaticText "shrinker_register()"
            - StaticText "/"
            - code
              - StaticText "shrinker_free()"
            - StaticText " on a dynamically allocated pointer ("
            - code
              - StaticText "linux/shrinker.h"
            - StaticText ")"
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Fixed all three, and hit a fourth issue at link time: "
          - code
            - StaticText "deps.c"
          - StaticText "'s "
          - code
            - StaticText "kallsyms_lookup_name()"
          - StaticText "-based lookup of the internal "
          - code
            - StaticText "shmem_zero_setup"
          - StaticText " symbol fails, because "
          - code
            - StaticText "kallsyms_lookup_name"
          - StaticText " itself is no longer exported to modules. Worked around it with the standard modern replacement: register a "
          - code
            - StaticText "kprobe"
          - StaticText " directly on the target symbol name and read the resolved address back out of "
          - code
            - StaticText "kp.addr"
          - StaticText ", then immediately unregister — this works because kprobe symbol resolution isn't restricted the way direct kallsyms lookup is."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "With this, "
          - code
            - StaticText "ashmem_linux.ko"
          - StaticText " builds cleanly and loads without error on kernel 6.17 (Ubuntu 24.04 GCE image) — "
          - code
            - StaticText "/dev/ashmem"
          - StaticText " appears, "
          - code
            - StaticText "dmesg"
          - StaticText " shows a clean "
          - code
            - StaticText "ashmem: initialized"
          - StaticText ", and Android 16 boots completely (verified: real home screen, real Settings app, zero FATAL/SIGSEGV/SIGABRT anywhere in the boot log — the SwiftShader graphics abort I was separately chasing in "
          - link "#934" [ref=e77]
          - StaticText " never happens at all once ashmem is actually working, which strongly suggests that crash was partly/wholly downstream of gralloc's buffer allocation failing without real shared memory, not a pure, independent SwiftShader limitation)."
        - paragraph
          - StaticText "Happy to open a PR against "
          - code
            - StaticText "redroid-modules"
          - StaticText " with the patch if useful — didn't want to assume that's wanted without asking first."
